clue.text: Section of pitches Boca Juniors turned over for sheep

indicators.note: turned over means the run of letters is read the other way round
a section of these words is a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: the run spans the end of pitches, all of Boca and the start of Juniors

explanation.surface: A football commentator describes a stretch of Boca Juniors' pitches being dug up for grazing sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Boca Juniors is a famous Argentine football club, which makes 'pitches' look like playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is a rare breed of piebald, many-horned sheep, so Jacobs is a plural for several of them.

clue.text: Joky judge left us squirming

indicators.note: squirming suggests wriggling about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A judge's joke leaves the court squirming in embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Jestful is an uncommon adjective for full of jests, which is the same as jokey or playful.

clue.text: My hair cut for holiday destination?

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!

indicators.note: cut means the hair word loses its final letter, as if trimmed short

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair

explanation.surface: Someone ponders getting a haircut before going away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive but an exclamation; COR is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island popular with British tourists, an example of a place people go on holiday.

clue.text: Clattery machine fillets fish before fishmonger's closing

parts.note: to bone a fish is to fillet it, so fillets gives bones as a verb
hake is a fish of the cod family
the closing letter of the word fishmonger, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: A noisy contraption at the fish counter fillets fish before the shop shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A boneshaker is an old bicycle with solid tyres, notorious for a rattling ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The early nineteenth-century bicycle earned its nickname from its jarring, noisy ride over cobbles, so it is a rattling contraption.

clue.text: Half of ingenious solution to lose weight, removing cream?

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: clever means ingenious

indicators.note: to lose means a letter is dropped from the solution word

parts.note: an answer is a solution

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a clever diet plan, wondering if cutting out cream would help them lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing cream' is read as a cream that removes: a cleanser takes off make-up. CLE is half of CLEVER, and ANSWER without W is ANSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is a cosmetic lotion used for taking off make-up and dirt, hence a cream for removing things.

clue.text: Ray technically produced beer that's special rather than good

indicators.note: rather than means one letter takes the place of another in the beer word

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A brewer boasts of a special beer rather than merely a good one.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is a device that generates an intense narrow beam of light, a ray made by technology.

clue.text: Ace mother's half of perfect couple

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a dam is the mother of an animal; the 's stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A proud mother boasts that her son is one half of the ideal couple.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve were the first pair in Eden, so he is one partner of an ideal pairing.

clue.text: Irrational ceremony starts with second song

indicators.note: starts with means the second piece goes at the very front

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
a ritual is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A strange rite opens with a second hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like an adjective for the ceremony, but it is a noun here: pi, a number that cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritual is a religious folk song from the African American tradition, a kind of song.

clue.text: Electronic lifts connected to circuits go wrong again

indicators.note: lifts means the electronic letter supports the rest from underneath, at the foot of this down entry

parts.note: re means about or concerning, i.e. connected to
laps are circuits of a track
E is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Electronic lifts linked up to their wiring keep breaking down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lifts' puts E underneath, holding up RE plus LAPS. The surface makes you think of elevators.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into an earlier bad state, such as illness or bad habits, after improving.

clue.text: Dog that's well trained asleep in back of car

parts.note: a spring is a well, a source of water

indicators.note: trained means these letters are drilled into a new order

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: its last letter joins the fodder

explanation.surface: A well-trained dog sleeps in the back of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well trained' looks like one phrase; split it. Rearrange ASLEEP IN plus R, the back of car, to give ERSPANIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a gundog breed used to flush game, an example of a dog.

clue.text: English character in Athens behind mirror

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
late means behind, as in behind schedule

explanation.surface: An English visitor in Athens lingers behind a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to copy or imitate them, as a verb meaning to reflect their behaviour.

clue.text: Resolute as engineers on rowing boats

indicators.note: on means the following pieces come after the boats in an across answer

parts.note: fours are rowing boats for four oarsmen
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers stay firm while sitting in rowing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursquare describes someone firm and unwavering, standing solidly, which matches being determined.

clue.text: Like half-sized member?

indicators.note: half-sized means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about the state of a shrunken body part.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a sly definition: a member at half size is floppy. LI is half of LIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy or lacking firmness, which is what a shrunken member would be in the rude reading.

clue.text: Playwright acts oddly cutting a little Scotch egg

indicators.note: cutting means the odd letters slice into the middle of the whisky and egg pieces

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of Scotch whisky
to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: oddly means take the first and third letters

parts.note: its odd letters are used

explanation.surface: A dramatist behaves strangely, slicing a Scotch egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch egg' (a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat) is a false unit: Scotch belongs with 'a little', and egg is a verb. The odd letters of acts, AT, cut DRAM from URGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a writer or adapter of plays, so a dramatist, a kind of writer for the stage.

clue.text: Cycling through 'The Greatest Country on the Med'

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter is moved round to the end

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, called himself The Greatest
by means through, as in by way of

explanation.surface: A slogan for a cycling tour across the best country on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: ALIBY with its A taken from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African nation with a long Mediterranean coastline.

clue.text: British have no armour, so bleed cruelly

parts.note: to lack is to have no
mail is chain armour

explanation.surface: Unarmoured British soldiers are wounded and bleed badly.
explanation.walkthrough: To bleed someone is to extort money from them; 'cruelly' sharpens it into threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is extortion by threats of exposure, a ruthless way of draining a victim of money.

clue.text: Couple in Audi sped around abroad giving way for French drivers

parts.note: the first couple of letters of Audi

indicators.note: around means the speeding word wraps round the abroad word

parts.note: tore means sped
out means abroad, out of the house

explanation.surface: A pair in an Audi race about overseas, yielding to French motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: An autoroute is a French motorway, the road network used by drivers in France.

clue.text: Saviour cleaves to cross

indicators.note: cleaves to here means splits the word to, sitting inside it

parts.note: an angel can be a saviour, someone who rescues

explanation.surface: A believer clings devotedly to the cross of the Saviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaves to' looks like clings to, but cleave also means split, and here the saviour splits TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a hybrid citrus fruit, a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo.

clue.text: Very adaptable fellow demands honey in tea, period

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
mel is the Latin and pharmacists' term for honey
an eon is a vast period of time

explanation.surface: A flexible man insists on honey in his tea, full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a lizard that changes colour, hence figuratively a person who adapts to any company.

clue.text: Punch comedian's jaw

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
a wag is a joker; the 's stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A comedian on the receiving end of a punch on the jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaw' looks like the body part, but it is a verb or noun for chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is a chat or gossip, and to jaw is informally to talk at length.

clue.text: Broil some leeks after discarding outer layers

indicators.note: stripping the outer layers of the phrase, two letters at each end like leek skins, leaves a run lying inside it

parts.note: the phrase whose inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: A recipe step: grill some leeks once the tough outer layers are peeled off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broil' looks like a cooking verb, but it is an old noun for a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A broil is an archaic word for a noisy quarrel, and a melee is a confused fight.

clue.text: Wrathful senior tails Henry out of bounds

indicators.note: tails means the senior piece follows behind
out of bounds means the word's boundary letters are dropped, leaving the middle

parts.note: its inner letters are used
aged means old, senior

explanation.surface: An elderly man follows Henry, who has wandered off limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraged means furious, full of anger, which is what wrathful also describes.

clue.text: Where bluegrass is black?

parts.note: where something is means the place it is in, so in
Kentucky is the Bluegrass State, postal abbreviation KY

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where grass could ever be black.
explanation.walkthrough: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky, the Bluegrass State, known for bluegrass country music.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means as dark as ink, an informal word for pitch black.

clue.text: You won't be quick, travelling in his car

definitions.text: You won't be quick, travelling in his car

parts.words: You won't be quick, travelling in his car
parts.note: quick also means alive, and the passenger in this vehicle is dead; the hearse also travels slowly

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain driver's car is slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' in the old sense of living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral director drives the hearse that carries the deceased, who are no longer living.

clue.text: Set up tablets and drip?

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means the pieces are written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so Es are ecstasy tablets
a run is a drip, as of paint

explanation.surface: A medical task list: lay out the pills and fix up an IV.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the job: someone who sets up tablets and a drip for a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is the hospital worker who gives medication and attends to patients' intravenous lines.

clue.text: Dumpling dip that's flipping hot

indicators.note: flipping means the dip word is turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: to sink is to dip
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the sauce for a dumpling is flipping hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but signals turning SINK over.
explanation.definitionFit: A knish is an Eastern European Jewish snack of dough filled with potato, akin to a dumpling.

clue.text: Mum rings off!

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence
O is ring-shaped, so OO is two rings

explanation.surface: Mother hangs up the phone with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the adjective meaning silent, as in keep mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is an exclamation used to drive someone away, like telling them to go away.

clue.text: Wood outside the house had big rowan tree spreading

indicators.note: spreading suggests the branches sprawling out, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A homeowner had a big rowan tree growing out over the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Weatherboarding is overlapping timber cladding on exterior walls, a wooden covering for the exterior of a building.

clue.text: Filly, one that's running

parts.note: filly is old slang for a girl, a gal
a loper runs with a long stride

explanation.surface: A young horse described simply as a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a filly is a young female racehorse, one that gallops.
explanation.definitionFit: A galloper is a horse that runs at full speed, and a racing filly is just such an animal.

clue.text: Routine amphetamine overdose

parts.note: meth is short for methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A habitual drug user's regular overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a set procedure or system, so a routine way of doing things.
